topic: Japan has the most centenarians of any country: 99,763 people aged 100+ as of 1 September 2025 (Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare), about 88% of them women; the first survey in 1963 counted 153. That is roughly 80 per 100,000 people. The United States counted about 80,000 centenarians in the 2020 census (about 24–30 per 100,000); China is estimated at roughly 50,000–60,000 (UN WPP 2024), under 5 per 100,000, despite ten times Japan's population. Okinawa is known for longevity. Since 1963 the government has given each new centenarian a silver sake cup; in 2016 it switched to silver-plated because of the cost of rising numbers.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The country with the most people must have the most centenarians — China.
myths.reality: China has roughly 50,000–60,000 people aged 100+; Japan, with a tenth of the population, has nearly 100,000.
